newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says six consortia in Toluca natgas bidding.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says six consortia in Toluca natgas bidding.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said Thursday it had six consortia making economic bids to distribute natural gas in Toluca.
The groups of companies passed the initial presentation of their technical proposals for the distribution concession, the CRE said in a statement.
--Mexico's Centra Gas de Toluca, Canada's WestCoast Energy Inc. and U.S. Coastal Gas Toluca
--France's Gaz de France and Mexico's Mexigas
--Mexico's Consorcio Sistema Automatico de Gas, Toluca Disco Holding and U.S. Enova Corp.
--Mexico's Grupo Mexicano de Desarollo, Canada's Gas International, and U.S. Shell Oil Company
--U.S. Noram Energy Corp and Mexico's Gutsa Construcciones
Toluca is the fourth and largest to date in a series of natural gas distribution rights sales. A total $100 million investment is expected for the region.
A decision on the winning bid is scheduled for July 29.

Mexico is privatizing its distribution of natural gas in a bid to increase use of the fuel and improve its infrastructure. Exploration is still controlled by state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
